purpose: Defines the requirements for the ADR writer, an isolated agent that judges, corrects, and records ADRs from requests, returning a create, reject, or insufficient verdict.
summary: Overview: an isolated ADR writer separates ADR judgment and writing from the design context
Terminology: request types (approval record, judgment record, update) and verdicts (create, reject, insufficient)
FNC-001/002: accepting typed requests and rejecting judgment records that do not merit an ADR
FNC-003/004: fixing malformed content before writing, and returning what is missing instead of inventing facts
FNC-005: approval records are never rejected; checked only for a valid reason and a verbatim user approval quote
FNC-006: updating a rejected decision by rewriting the same section and moving the old option into alternatives
FNC-007: returning a verdict value that callers can branch on, with reasons only for reject and insufficient
FNC-008/009: one ADR file per feature under adr/, numbered once, with writes limited to the ADR file
FNC-010/011/012: single entry point, start-design holds no ADR norms, norms centralized in one document
NFR: context isolation and visible failure when the writer cannot finish
tasks: Implementing or modifying the ADR writer agent or its entry skill
Designing the ADR writer in a design document
Requesting an approval record from start-design
Deciding whether a decision should be recorded as an ADR
Updating or overturning an existing ADR decision
Determining ADR file placement and numbering
